correctness.rationale: In the full order-m closure of polyanalytic polynomials, each positive-frequency sector z^k P(|z|²) (deg P≤m−1) is finite-dimensional and its cutoff Rayleigh quotient is Q_k(P). For each nonzero P, increasing k size-biases s toward 1, strictly reducing mass on (0,R). Positivity a.e. of w gives a strictly negative covariance; compactness of projective polynomial space makes the gap uniform, and Courant–Fischer yields λ_j(k+1)<λ_j(k) for all j. Negative-frequency sectors embed into the +h polynomial sector and hence do not maximize. For m=2, w=1, exact 2×2 Gram determinants/traces give roots Λk± with product R^(2k+4); p0(R²)=−4R³(1−R)² and p1(R²)=−8R⁴(1−R)² establish leading separation from the negative mode R². Eigenvectors yield the sharp projection gap. Formal expansion gives Δ~4R as R↓0 and 3/4(1−R)^3 as R↑1. Independent SymPy replay checked tr/det and polynomial straddles.
residual_risks: Only centered initial radial interval and positive a.e. weight. Explicit Λk± and gap apply to the unweighted bianalytic full space, not all weights.

value.rationale: An all-order centered-disk concentration problem is a natural norm/localization question. The strict size-bias ordering proves radial rigidity of all maximizers for arbitrary positive weights; the unweighted bianalytic second eigenvalue and cubic stability gap quantify the sharp global deficit and equality space. These conclusions are not automatic from the known individual matrices.
residual_risks: Does not cover annular windows, arbitrary disconnected radial cutoff sets or full true-polyanalytic summands as separate spaces.
